anti_overlap: Focuses on qualification cost, integration risk, and NRE accounting — not venue/platform fit (fd-theatrical-production-touring), not system load profile matching (fd-building-systems-commissioning), not sketch-to-spec prototype epistemology (fd-industrial-design-sketch-to-spec)
decision_lens: Is the rendering stack reuse decision being evaluated with make-buy discipline — explicit qualification cost for the off-the-shelf component, explicit integration risk for bringing it into the new system, and explicit fallback if qualification fails? Or is reuse being chosen because it feels cheaper without that analysis?
distance_rationale: Aerospace make-buy analysis is the most rigorous professional discipline for the reuse-vs-build decision — it has explicit methods for qualification cost, integration risk, NRE accounting, obsolescence risk, and prototype-as-qualification. These map directly to renderer stack selection when applied at the right abstraction level.
expected_isomorphisms: COTS component → sibling project renderer. Qualification cost → adaptation/porting effort. System specification → rendering requirements document. Integration risk → API coupling analysis. NRE → development cost for each option. EDU phase → prototype sprint with go/no-go criteria. Component obsolescence → sibling project divergence risk.
focus: Make-vs-buy analysis for aircraft subsystems, qualification cost of COTS components vs. bespoke development, integration risk when third-party components enter a certified system
name: fd-aerospace-make-buy-subsystem
persona: Systems engineer at an aerospace OEM with 22 years of avionics and structural subsystem procurement, trained in DO-178 qualification and FAA/EASA certification pathways for component reuse
review_areas: Qualification cost of COTS component: aerospace make-buy analysis counts the cost of qualifying a COTS component for the new system — for the sibling renderer, what is the cost to qualify it for the colony sim's requirements (performance envelopes, 2D assumptions, native platform behavior)?

Integration risk delta: integrating a third-party subsystem introduces interface risk, schedule risk, and defect attribution complexity — does the sibling renderer's codebase have the modularity to integrate cleanly, or will it require invasive modification that destroys the benefit of reuse?

Non-recurring engineering (NRE) honest accounting: make-buy analysis distinguishes recurring unit cost from NRE — what is the NRE to adapt the sibling renderer vs. the NRE to build fresh? NRE is often underestimated for COTS adaptation.

Component obsolescence risk: COTS avionics components are deprecated; the sibling project may evolve independently — does reusing the sibling renderer create a long-term maintenance coupling where both projects must stay in sync?

Specification compliance before selection: aerospace OEMs require a component to meet the system specification before purchase order — is there a formal specification for the colony sim's rendering requirements against which each option is evaluated, or is the decision being made before the spec exists?

Risk-reduction prototyping as qualification: aerospace uses engineering development units (EDUs) to qualify components before production commitment — does the hybrid prototype→production path function as a proper EDU phase with go/no-go criteria, or is it an open-ended exploration without commitment criteria?

severity_examples.condition: No documented FPS target, tile count budget, platform minimum spec, or 2D rendering feature list before evaluating options
severity_examples.scenario: Reuse decision made without a rendering requirements specification — qualification cannot be assessed because the target performance envelope is undefined

severity_examples.condition: No explicit API boundary defined between the colony sim's ECS and the reused renderer; direct internal API usage
severity_examples.scenario: Sibling renderer integrated without interface isolation — a defect or evolution in the sibling project propagates directly into the colony sim's rendering path

severity_examples.condition: Make-buy analysis used optimistic integration estimates without a comparable fresh-build NRE estimate
severity_examples.scenario: NRE for COTS adaptation exceeds the NRE estimate for fresh build after 3 months of integration work

source_domain: Aerospace systems engineering and make-buy analysis
success_hints: Check whether the decision analysis includes a parallel cost estimate for the fresh-build option that is as detailed as the reuse option's cost estimate. Make-buy analysis is only valid when both sides of the ledger are measured with equal rigor. If the fresh-build estimate is a single number and the reuse estimate is a detailed breakdown, the analysis is biased.
task_context: Choosing a rendering stack for a native Rust colony sim. Options span: reusing a proven sibling project renderer vs. building fresh vs. lighter frameworks vs. hybrid prototype→production. Core tension: proven reuse vs. 2D-first design without 3D baggage.
